title: Integral equivariant coherent Grothendieck groups and canonical operations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $G$ be a group object over $S$ [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $Y$ be an $S$-scheme with action $a:G\times_SY\to Y$. Present the action groupoid with source $p=\operatorname{pr}_2$, target $a$, identity $(1,y)$, inverse $(g^{-1},gy)$ and composition $(g,h,y)\mapsto(gh,y)$, satisfying the scheme-groupoid laws [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. A coherent linearized module is an object of the recorded groupoid-module category [def-sfb-scheme-groupoid-module] whose underlying module is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Thus its isomorphism is $a^*M\simeq p^*M$ and satisfies the identity and actual pullback cocycle; the inverse gives the geometric action from $y$ to $gy$. Define $G_0^G(Y)$ as the quotient of the free abelian group on these objects by the subgroup generated by $[M]-[N]$ for equivariant isomorphisms and $[B]-[A]-[C]$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. For the following operations specify a representative by an underlying isomorphism intertwining the indicated linearizations, using the canonical composition comparisons of module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Tensor uses the existing sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and its section-normalized pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. For an equivariant map $i:W\to Y$, pullback has its induced square on $G\times_SW$; pushforward is characterized by an equivariant map $i^*M\to N$ whose adjoint $M\to i_*N$ is invertible. The unit is $\mathcal O_Y$ with its structure-sheaf linearization, using the adjoint structure-sheaf morphism [def-sfb-tensor-pullback-structure-sheaf-map]. For an invariant closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], its ideal is the actual kernel ideal module included equivariantly in this unit. Exterior power is the sheafification of the sectionwise exterior power, with pullback comparisons pinned on wedges and with the linearization carrying each wedge to the wedge of the linearized sections. These are operation predicates, not arbitrary choices of objects or maps.
